description: The preferences a principal holds, and what each may be set to. spec-10 §20 forbids a code path supplying a value a registry omits, so a key's domain and its default are here and nowhere else. A `number` domain carries the step it moves by as well as its bounds: a bound and a default do not say how finely a person may move between them, and a control choosing its own increment would be a set of settable values the registry never stated. Each is the coarsest increment whose effect is visible, so every position a control offers is a setting a person can tell from its neighbours.

theme.description: Which ramp the interface draws from. `system` is the third state A.10.1 requires be kept rather than resolved away, so what is stored is the person's intent and the resolved value is computed where it is rendered.

contrast.description: §14.5 names a contrast preference among the five that disclose a disability.

motion.description: §14.5 names a motion preference. §17.8 makes it govern more than duration: under it, transform animation, parallax, auto-advance and automatic preview are disabled whatever else is set.

density.description: A.1.6 gives density its values and no section says where a person's choice lives, so holding it here is this deployment's decision rather than a requirement. There is no media feature for how tightly a person wants things packed, so it has no `system` state.

text_size.description: §14.5 names a text size among the five. A proportion of the root size rather than a step, because A.1.3 has a rem honour the browser font size a person has already set and a step would discard it. 100 leaves that setting alone.

described_audio.description: §14.5 names a described-audio default among the five. Whether a described audio track is chosen where a holding carries one.

automatic_preview.description: §17.8: automatic preview of a holding on hover or focus "MUST default off, MUST be a per-principal preference, MUST be suppressed under reduced motion regardless of that preference". The suppression is not stored; it is read from the motion preference where a preview would start.

next_member_offer.description: §12.4 requires the end-of-item offer "be disableable per principal" and states no default. It is on, because the section makes the offer the behaviour and disabling it the choice.

language.description: The languages whose names this principal prefers, held as the language range spec-01 §7.4's resolution profile carries. A nomen's tag is matched against it by [RFC4647] §3.3.1 basic filtering rather than string equality, so `en` is matched by `en`, `en-GB` and `en-Latn-GB`. A request naming `language` narrows that request only and does not change what is held here. `empty_request` is what a request naming `language` with no value asks for: naming the parameter asks to be narrowed, and an empty value names no range to narrow by, so the deployment's own language answers.

caption_face.description: §17.4 requires caption presentation "be adjustable by the person, persisted per principal" and names no property of it, so these four are what this deployment draws. A caption is set in the same three families the rest of the interface has.

caption_size.description: A proportion of the caption's own base, which ranges further than body text because a caption is read at whatever distance the picture is watched from.

caption_ground.description: What sits behind the glyphs. A caption is drawn over moving picture rather than over a surface, so no contrast floor can be met by the ink alone: the ground is what makes one meetable, and removing it is a choice with `caption_edge` as its compensation.

caption_edge.description: How a glyph separates from the picture where the ground does not do it. Idle where the ground is solid.

audio_language.description: Which language's audio this principal prefers, as a language range matched by [RFC4647] §3.3.1 basic filtering. §8.6 makes this orthogonal to naming: a household name in one language and personal audio in another is coherent and must be supported, so this is not the `language` key the resolution profile reads. `any` expresses no preference, and the selection then answers the expression nearest the work's canonical form.

subtitle_language.description: Which language's subtitles this principal prefers, matched as `audio_language` is. §8.6 keeps audio selection, subtitle selection and subtitle visibility independent and forbids collapsing them into a single language preference.

subtitle_visibility.description: Whether subtitles are shown. `foreign_audio` shows them where the audio the selection chose is not in the language this principal reads, which is the case they are most often wanted for and the one a switch makes a person answer by hand every time. The default is `off`, which is this deployment's: §8.6 states none, and a setting that turns subtitles on unasked is the interface deciding.

reading_face.description: The face long-form text is set in. The three families the token file holds, and `serif` is the default because the token file gives that family as "Long-form reading and a scan's transcript". A.3.6 permits a face marketed for dyslexia among the choices, and forbids it being a default or labelled an accessibility feature: [DYSLEXIA-META] pools fifteen studies over 688 readers and finds no reliable effect on reading speed or accuracy.

reading_size.description: A proportion of long-form text's own base. A.3.6 requires the size be settable and bounds it nowhere, so the bound is this deployment's: the range a caption takes, because long-form text is magnified further than the interface around it — A.3.6's own warning that hyphenation "harms magnified reading" assumes as much.

reading_line_height.description: The leading of long-form text, as a multiple of its own size. A.3.6 gives 1.55 for `sys.type.body.md`, which is the default. The floor is 1.15, the tightest line height the annex states anywhere (`sys.type.display.*`); the ceiling is this deployment's.

reading_measure.description: How far a line of long-form text runs, counted in characters of the face it is set in. A.3.6 asks for a short measure and states no figure, so the range and the default are this deployment's.

reading_letter_spacing.description: Added to the face's own letter spacing. A.3.6 asks for generous spacing and states no figure; 0 is the face's own spacing, which is where it starts, and the ceiling is this deployment's.

reading_word_spacing.description: Added to the face's own word spacing. 0 is the face's own spacing, and the ceiling is this deployment's.

reading_alignment.description: A.3.6 gives the default as `start` and justification as off, because justification without hyphenation produces rivers. Two values, because centring or ending long-form text is a display treatment rather than a reading choice.

reading_hyphenation.description: A.3.6 gives the default as off: hyphenation fragments words across lines, which harms magnified reading. It is what makes justification legible, so a reader choosing `justify` is the one who wants it.

reading_theme.description: Which ramp long-form text draws from, which A.3.6 makes a choice of its own rather than the interface's. `interface` takes whatever the interface resolved, so reading needs no second answer to the system signal; the other two are A.1.6's theme contexts.

browse_continue.description: §9.2: "A mode MAY be hidden per principal. Hiding a mode MUST NOT hide content." One key per mode rather than a list, because §9.2 fixes the seven and a key each keeps the set closed in the database. Continue is the requesting principal's own resume list.

browse_places.description: Places, as a list and as a map.

browse_time.description: A spine over time-spans, with a counted Undated bucket.
